title: Enter-key handler bypasses the disabled-button guard, allowing concurrent (paid) council runs
description: councilRun() guards against double-submit only by disabling the Run Council button (runBtn.disabled=true at 4774, re-enabled in finally at 4792). But the symbol input's keyup handler at line 4810 (`if (e.key === 'Enter') councilRun()`) calls councilRun() directly and never checks whether a run is already in flight or whether the button is disabled. Pressing Enter repeatedly (or Enter then clicking) launches multiple overlapping fetches to /api/aj/council/<symbol>. Each council run invokes the LLM and incurs real cost_usd, so this is a money-spending defect, not just a UI glitch. The two in-flight runs also race to write resEl.innerHTML and to call councilLoadRecent(), producing out-of-order results.
fix: Add a module/closure-scoped in-flight flag instead of relying on the button. At the top of councilRun: `if (councilBusy) return; councilBusy = true;` and reset it in the finally block (`councilBusy = false;`). Declare `let councilBusy = false;` alongside the const declarations. The keyup handler then no-ops while a run is active.

title: Scanner results inject symbol/catalysts/tags into innerHTML and onclick without escaping
description: renderScanResults() and the _scannerTopCard/_scannerSignalCard helpers interpolate o.symbol, o.catalysts, o.tags, and o.asset_type straight into HTML and into onclick="openResearch('...')" with no _esc/_jesc. Every other render path in this file escapes API text. A catalyst string containing a double-quote breaks the title="..." attribute (line 7545) and a symbol/catalyst containing markup or a single quote either injects HTML or produces a SyntaxError that no-ops the click. This is the exact 'inject un-escaped API text via innerHTML' class the codebase has repeatedly hit.
fix: Wrap text sinks in _esc() and onclick arguments in _jesc(): e.g. onclick="openResearch('"+_jesc(o.symbol)+"')" and >'+_esc(o.symbol)+'<, _esc((o.catalysts||[]).join(', ')) for both the cell text and the title attribute, and _esc(t) for each tag badge in the .map at 7529.

title: Fundamentals: genuine 0% values render as '—' (falsy-zero ternary)
description: In renderFundamentals(), many percentage rows use the pattern `fmt.pct(fund.revenue_growth ? fund.revenue_growth * 100 : null)` (revenue_growth, earnings_growth, profit_margin, gross_margin, operating_margin, return_on_equity, return_on_assets, dividend_yield, payout_ratio, short_percent_float). Because `0` is falsy, a company with a legitimate 0% value (e.g. 0% revenue growth, 0% payout ratio, 0 short float) takes the `: null` branch and shows '—' instead of '0.00%'. The backend supplies these as fractions (yfinance), so 0 is a real, distinguishable value. Note the sibling renderFundamentalsStrip() correctly uses `!= null`, making the two views inconsistent.
fix: Replace the truthy check with an explicit null check, e.g. `['Revenue Growth', fund.revenue_growth != null ? fmt.pct(fund.revenue_growth * 100) : '—']`, applied to every `X ? X*100 : null` line. Or add a small helper `const pct100 = v => v != null ? fmt.pct(v*100) : '—';`.

title: Agent paper-positions table prints 'undefined%'/'null%' if unrealized_pct or weight_pct is missing
description: In loadTradingView's positions render, the row uses ${p.unrealized_pct>=0?'+':''}${_esc(String(p.unrealized_pct))}% and ${_esc(String(p.weight_pct))}%. The backend (aj_analytics.positions_detail) currently always supplies numeric defaults (0.0), but the row has no null guard: any position object that omits these keys (e.g. a future/legacy shape, or a partial book) renders the literal text 'undefined%' / 'null%', and the color ternary (p.unrealized_pct||0)>=0 silently falls to green. This is the exact class of fragile cell the rest of the file guards (see _ajMoney/_ajPct).
fix: Reuse the existing _ajPct helper for the percent cells: replace `${p.unrealized_pct>=0?'+':''}${_esc(String(p.unrealized_pct))}%` with `${p.unrealized_pct==null?'—':(p.unrealized_pct>=0?'+':'')+_esc(String(p.unrealized_pct))+'%'}` and `${_esc(String(p.weight_pct))}%` with `${p.weight_pct==null?'—':_esc(String(p.weight_pct))+'%'}`.

title: buildSignalCard throws if a score object lacks a symbol, blanking the whole Signals grid
description: cardId = 'ml-panel-' + s.symbol.replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g, '') dereferences s.symbol unconditionally. renderSignalsGrid maps every score through buildSignalCard with .join(''); if any single score object is missing .symbol (null/undefined), .replace throws and the entire grid render aborts, leaving the Signals view empty even though most rows were valid. addSignalSymbol() pushes a raw API object straight into _signalsCache, so a malformed single-symbol response also poisons the cached grid.
fix: Guard at the top of buildSignalCard: `const sym = s && s.symbol ? String(s.symbol) : ''; if (!sym) return ''; const cardId = 'ml-panel-' + sym.replace(/[^A-Z0-9]/g,'');` and use sym thereafter.

title: Reflexivity detector renders dominant loop, direction, timeline, detail and fundamentals unescaped
description: detectReflexivity() builds the KPI cards and per-loop cards by concatenating data.dominant_loop (dominant), loop.direction, loop.acceleration_timeline (timeline), loop.detail (detail), and every fundamentals_snapshot value/key into innerHTML with no _esc. These come from the /api/reflexivity API. Inconsistent with the escaped sinks elsewhere; any '<' in these strings injects markup.
fix: Escape each interpolation: _esc(dominant), _esc(direction || '—'), _esc(timeline), _esc(detail), and _esc(fundamentals[fKeys[f]]) / _esc(fKeys[f].replace(...)).

title: Synthetic-insider signal, channel name/detail and portfolio symbol rendered unescaped
description: analyzeSyntheticInsider() injects data.signal (signal), ch.channel/ch.name, and ch.detail directly into innerHTML; scanSyntheticInsiderPortfolio() injects it.symbol/it.ticker into both a table cell and an onclick handler unescaped (line 8358). All from /api/synthetic-insider. Unescaped API text in innerHTML/onclick.
fix: Use _esc(signal), _esc(ch.channel||ch.name||'—'), _esc(ch.detail||'—'); for the portfolio row use _jesc inside the onclick and _esc in the cell text for it.symbol/it.ticker.

title: Liquidity monitor recommendation, indicator name, value and detail rendered unescaped
description: loadLiquidityData() concatenates data.recommendation, ind.indicator/ind.name, ind.value, and ind.detail (all from /api/liquidity) into innerHTML without _esc, while sibling code escapes equivalent fields.
fix: Escape: _esc(recommendation), _esc(ind.indicator||ind.name||'—'), _esc(ind.value), _esc(ind.detail||'—').

title: Alt-data nowcast confidence, signal name/detail and portfolio scan symbol/signal unescaped
description: nowcastAltData() injects data.confidence_level (confidence), sig.signal/sig.name and sig.detail unescaped; scanAltDataPortfolio() injects it.symbol/it.ticker into an onclick (line 8865) and it.signal into a cell (8868) unescaped. All from /api/alt-data.
fix: Wrap with _esc() for text cells and _jesc() for the onclick symbol argument; e.g. _esc(confidence), _esc(sig.signal||sig.name||'—'), _esc(sig.detail||'—'), _esc(it.signal||'—').

title: Narrative window breakdown can render '[object Object]' rows
description: In analyzeNarrative() the window breakdown does buckets = wData.buckets || wData.distribution || wData. When a window object has neither buckets nor distribution, buckets falls through to the entire window object (wData), so Object.keys() iterates metadata keys (e.g. velocity, label) and prints _esc(buckets[k]) which may itself be an object, rendering '[object Object]'. The intended bucket distribution is lost.
fix: Only fall back to a known bucket-bearing field: buckets = wData.buckets || wData.distribution || null; and guard `if (buckets && typeof buckets==='object')` so non-distribution window objects render nothing instead of dumping all keys.

title: Forecast ensemble shows 'NaN%' when prob/consensus fields are missing
description: analyzeForecast() computes probPct=Math.round(ens.prob_up*100), probRawPct=Math.round(ens.prob_up_raw*100), consensusPct=Math.round(ens.consensus*100) with no null guard. If the ensemble omits any of these (e.g. a thin-data symbol that still returns an ensemble object), Math.round(undefined*100) yields NaN and the hero gauge renders 'NaN%' plus a width:NaN% bar. The code already guards `if (!ens) throw`, but not the individual fields.
fix: Coerce/guard each: var probPct = ens.prob_up!=null ? Math.round(ens.prob_up*100) : null; and render (probPct!=null?probPct+'%':'—') with width:(probPct||0)%. Same for prob_up_raw and consensus.

title: Inline research-button rewiring runs before app.js defines window.openResearch, breaking the quick buttons
description: The trailing inline <script> (not deferred, no DOMContentLoaded wrap) rewrites each #view-research button's onclick to `new Function(... .replace('openResearch','window.openResearch'))` and runs synchronously at parse time. All the real scripts (app.js etc.) use defer, so they execute AFTER this inline script. At rewrite time window.openResearch/window.openCryptoResearch are undefined — the Function body still references them, so it only resolves at click time, which is fine — BUT the .replace only swaps the FIRST 'openResearch' occurrence and does nothing for the BTC button which calls openCryptoResearch (line 150). That button's rewritten handler calls bare openCryptoResearch (not window-qualified); if openCryptoResearch is not a global function declaration it throws ReferenceError on click.
fix: Either drop this inline rewrite entirely (the onclick attributes already call the globals) or make it robust: run inside DOMContentLoaded and replace all relevant names, e.g. .replace(/openResearch|openCryptoResearch/g, m=>'window.'+m), or simply leave the original onclick attributes untouched since app.js already exposes these as window globals.

title: Analyst band is HTML-escaped twice (_esc then _ajPill re-escapes)
description: _ajPill() already calls _esc() on its label argument (line 4230: `${_esc(label)}`). At line 4250 the caller passes `_ajPill(_esc(String(r.band || '—')), true, 'blue')`, escaping the band a second time. Any '&', '<', '"' or "'" in band text would render double-encoded (e.g. an '&' becomes '&amp;'). In practice band values are enum strings (e.g. VERY_BULLISH) with no special chars, so it is usually invisible, but it is a real correctness defect and the band column is documented as possibly a free-form label (aj_schemas.py:207 'or free band label'), which could contain special characters.
fix: Drop the inner _esc since _ajPill escapes internally: `${_ajPill(String(r.band || '—'), true, 'blue')}`. (This matches how dec.action is passed un-pre-escaped at line 4272.)

title: Recent-decisions endpoint is fetched on every trading-view render, even when the Council tab is never opened
description: councilLoadRecent() is invoked unconditionally at line 4811 at the end of loadTradingView(). loadTradingView() is re-run on initial load and again on every Refresh, Kill, Run-cycle, preset-apply, and config-save (each of those calls loadTradingView()). So /api/aj/council/recent (a DB query over aj_council_runs LIMIT 50) is hit on every one of those actions regardless of whether the user ever clicks the Council tab. The default active pane is 'dashboard', so the result is usually invisible. This is needless load.
fix: Lazy-load: only call councilLoadRecent() the first time the Council tab is activated. In the tab-switch handler (line 4546-4550), when the clicked pane is 'council' and it hasn't been loaded yet, call councilLoadRecent() once (guard with a `councilRecentLoaded` flag). Remove the unconditional call at 4811.

title: Analyst score rendered as a raw, unrounded float
description: Score is interpolated raw: `${r.score == null ? '—' : _esc(String(r.score)) + '/10'}`. The backend score is a REAL clamped to 0..10 (aj_schemas.py:208,215) and can come straight from an LLM or a band-derived value, so values like 6.6667 or 7.49999 will display as '6.6667/10'. The rest of the AJTA UI rounds numeric displays (e.g. win-rate Math.round(...*100)); the council card is inconsistent and can show long fractional tails.
fix: Format to at most one decimal: `${r.score == null ? '—' : (Math.round(Number(r.score)*10)/10) + '/10'}` (or Number(r.score).toFixed(1)).

title: _ajPct silently misreads a true 100% (value 1.0) vs a 1% value, by design heuristic
description: _ajPct treats any |value| <= 1 as a fraction and multiplies by 100. For the council this is safe today because conviction (aj_schemas.py:383) and confidence (4252) are always clamped to 0..1 on the backend. The risk is latent: if any future field feeding _ajPct is already expressed in percent and happens to be <= 1 (e.g. 0.8 meaning 0.8%), it will be shown as 80%. Flagging as a fragility in the new helper rather than a present-day break; conviction and confidence are correctly 0..1 so no current miscount.
fix: If feasible, make _ajPct explicit about the expected scale (pass a flag or always treat council inputs as fractions) rather than guessing from magnitude. At minimum add a code comment that callers must pass a 0..1 fraction.

title: KPI P&L shows '$-' for negative values (sign/$ ordering)
description: Overview UNREALIZED P&L (line 901: `${summary.total_pnl >= 0 ? '+' : ''}$${fmt.compact(summary.total_pnl)}`) and Portfolio TOTAL P&L (line 1136: `(summary.total_pnl >= 0 ? '+' : '') + '$' + fmt.currency(summary.total_pnl)`) prepend '$' before a value that fmt.compact/fmt.currency already renders with a leading minus, producing strings like `$-1.20K` / `$-1,200.00`. The position-row code (line 1073) does it correctly with `(v >= 0 ? '+$' : '-$') + fmt.currency(Math.abs(v))`, so the KPI cards are inconsistent and look broken on a losing portfolio.
fix: Mirror the row formatting: `${summary.total_pnl >= 0 ? '+$' : '-$'}${fmt.compact(Math.abs(summary.total_pnl))}` (and same for fmt.currency in the portfolio KPI).

title: Crypto 'Max Supply' never shows ∞ for uncapped coins
description: `['Max Supply', fmt.compact(coin.max_supply) || '∞']` — fmt.compact() returns the string '—' (not '' or null) when max_supply is null. '—' is truthy, so the `|| '∞'` fallback is dead code. Uncapped coins (e.g. ETH, DOGE) show '—' instead of the intended '∞'.
fix: Test the raw field before formatting: `['Max Supply', coin.max_supply != null ? fmt.compact(coin.max_supply) : '∞']`.

title: Triggered-alert toast double-escapes the symbol
description: _pollTriggeredAlerts builds `Toast.warn(`${dir} ALERT ${_esc(a.symbol)} @ ...`)`. Toast.show() already runs `_esc(msg)` over the whole string (line 204), so the symbol is escaped twice: an ampersand in a symbol becomes `&amp;` and an apostrophe `&#39;`, displaying the literal entity text. The pre-escaping here is both wrong and unnecessary.
fix: Pass the raw symbol: `Toast.warn(`${dir} ALERT ${a.symbol} @ ${cur} (target $${fmt.price(a.price)})`)` and rely on Toast.show's single _esc pass.

title: Add Position rejects a legitimate $0 cost basis
description: submitAddPosition guards with `if (!symbol || !shares || !cost)`. `!cost` is true when cost === 0, so a gifted/spun-off/zero-basis lot (avg_cost 0, a real scenario for cost-basis tracking) is rejected with 'Symbol, shares, and cost are required' even though the user filled everything in. shares 0 is correctly invalid, but cost 0 is valid.
fix: Validate cost separately allowing 0: `if (!symbol || !shares || isNaN(cost) || cost < 0) { Toast.warn(...); return; }` (require a non-empty numeric field rather than a truthy one).

title: Alert distance color compares null distance_pct against 0
description: In the active-alerts table, after `atTarget` (which null-checks), the distColor expression evaluates `(a.alert_type === 'above' && a.distance_pct < 0)` and `(... && a.distance_pct > 0)` even when `a.distance_pct == null`. With null, `null < 0` is false and `null > 0` is false, so it silently falls through to the default dim color — not a crash, but a missing-data row gets a misleading 'neutral' styling rather than being treated as unknown. The distance cell itself (line 2883) correctly guards `!= null`.
fix: Short-circuit on null first: `const distColor = a.distance_pct == null ? 'var(--text-dim)' : atTarget ? 'var(--amber)' : ...;`

title: Dividend per-share estimate divides annual rate by an assumed frequency
description: In the upcoming ex-dates list, when frequency is unknown/Irregular the code divides the annual div_rate by a hard-coded 4 (quarterly) to estimate per-share payment: `divisor = freqMap[freq] != null ? freqMap[freq] : 4`. For a monthly or semi-annual payer whose `frequency` string doesn't exactly match the freqMap keys ('Monthly'/'Quarterly'/'Semi-Annual'/'Annual' — case- and label-sensitive), the per-share figure is wrong by up to 3x while only flagging '(approx, freq unknown)'. Backend frequency labels must match these exact strings or every payer is mis-estimated.
fix: Normalize the frequency key (trim/lowercase and map synonyms) before lookup, and prefer a backend-provided per-share/last-dividend amount when available instead of deriving it from the annual rate.

title: Dividend monthly-income histogram computed but never rendered
description: loadDividendsView builds `months` (line 3079) and `monthlyIncome` (lines 3080-3088) by iterating every dividend position's history, but neither variable is referenced anywhere in the subsequent innerHTML template. This is pure wasted computation on every dividends refresh (and a likely sign a 'next 12 months' chart was dropped during a refactor). new Date(h.date) on a bad string also yields getMonth()===NaN, writing a stray 'NaN' property.
fix: Either render the monthly bar chart that this data was meant to feed, or delete the months/monthlyIncome block (lines 3079-3088) to avoid the dead loop.

title: Transactions fallback totals/rows can produce NaN when summary endpoint fails
description: When /api/transactions/summary fails, totals fall back to `txns.filter(...).reduce((s,t)=>s+t.total,0)`. If any transaction row has `total` undefined/null, the reduce yields NaN and the TOTAL BUY/SELL KPIs render '$NaN'. Similarly the per-row TOTAL cell `$${fmt.currency(t.total)}` is guarded by fmt (shows '—'), but the aggregate is not. The summary endpoint is the normal path, so this only surfaces when summary 200-fails.
fix: Coerce in the reducer: `reduce((s,t)=>s+(t.total||0),0)` for both total_buy and total_sell.

title: Sidebar watchlist change% color/value not null-guarded like the main table
description:
loadSidebarWatchlist renders `
${fmt.pct(i.change_pct)}
`. When the batch quote has no price (rate-limited / unknown symbol), change_pct is null: fmt.pct renders '—' (fine) but the class resolves to '' so a down move and a no-data row look identical, and there's no neutral/dim styling. Minor visual-correctness gap versus the full watchlist table which adds alert highlighting.
fix: Add a dim class for the null case, e.g. `i.change_pct == null ? 'flat' : i.change_pct > 0 ? 'up' : i.change_pct < 0 ? 'down' : 'flat'`.

title: News dedupe/sort drops items with missing/duplicate titles and unparseable dates
description: loadGlobalNews dedupes by `n.title` (line 2556) — any news item with a null/empty title collapses to a single entry (Set key undefined), and the sort `new Date(b.published) - new Date(a.published)` (2558) yields NaN comparisons for unparseable `published` strings, leaving those items in arbitrary order. Not a crash, but causes silently missing/mis-ordered headlines when a source omits a title or uses a non-ISO date.
fix: Key the Set on `n.title || n.url` and guard the sort: `(b,t)=>(new Date(t.published)||0)`-style with isNaN fallbacks so undated items sort last instead of jumbling.

title: Stress scenario object serialized into an inline onclick attribute
description: renderStressResults emits `onclick="showScenarioDetail('${_esc(_jesc(name))}', ${_esc(JSON.stringify(s))})"`, embedding the entire serialized scenario object (including its positions array and description text) as a literal JS expression inside the attribute. The escaping (_esc over the JSON so double-quotes survive as " inside the double-quoted attribute) is actually correct, but this is fragile: any future field containing a backslash, newline, or the substring `</` in description can still break attribute/JS parsing or HTML tokenization, and it bloats the DOM. It works today but is a latent break.
fix: Stop inlining the object: render `onclick="showScenarioDetail('${_jesc(name)}')"` and have showScenarioDetail look the scenario up from a module-scoped `_lastStressScenarios[name]` set in renderStressResults, instead of round-tripping JSON through an HTML attribute.

title: _ansiToHtml leaves unbalanced <span> tags for combined ANSI codes (e.g. \033[97;1m)
description: The terminal welcome banner and help text emit combined ANSI sequences like '\033[97m\033[1m' and the renderer also handles multi-code sequences by splitting on ';'. For a sequence such as 97;1 it opens TWO spans (one for 97, one for 1), but a reset '0' (\033[0m) only emits a single . Over a help screen this leaves nested, never-closed spans, so styling (color/bold/opacity) bleeds into subsequent lines and can leak past the term-result container.
fix: Track open-span depth and close all of them on reset: when code==='0' emit one per currently-open span (or wrap each ansi run so a single always balances). Simplest: count spans opened since the last reset and emit that many when a '0' is seen.

title: RUN CYCLE button error path resets label to wrong text ('▶ RUN CYCLE (paper)')
description: The run button is rendered with label '▶ RUN CYCLE' (line 4333). On a failed run the catch handler sets runBtn.textContent = '▶ RUN CYCLE (paper)' (line 4574), so after any run error the button permanently shows a different label than it started with until the view is reloaded. Cosmetic but visibly inconsistent.
fix: Change the catch reset on line 4574 to '▶ RUN CYCLE' to match the rendered label.

title: Settings → SYSTEM INFO hardcodes 'AUGUR v2.3.0' while the agent reports v3.4.0
description: The SYSTEM INFO panel renders a hardcoded version string 'AUGUR v2.3.0'. The trading agent status endpoint reports version 3.4.0 (aj_metrics.status) and the loadTradingView hero falls back to '3.0.0'. The Settings version is a stale literal that no longer reflects the app, which is misleading on a diagnostics panel.
fix: Either pull the version from a single source (e.g. /api/settings or a /api/version field) or update the literal to the current app version; avoid duplicating version strings across views.

title: Options chain strikeCls computed from a ternary whose both branches return '' (dead code)
description: const strikeCls = (call && call.inTheMoney) || (put && put.inTheMoney) ? '' : '' always evaluates to '' regardless of the condition, and strikeCls is never used in the row template. This is leftover dead code that misleads readers into thinking ITM strikes get a class; they do not.
fix: Remove the strikeCls line, or give the truthy branch a real class (e.g. 'options-strike-itm') and apply it to the strike <td>.

title: renderMLForecastPanel computes probDown but never renders it
description: const probDown = 100 - probUp; is computed (line 6552) but never used anywhere in the returned markup (only probUp is shown). Harmless but indicates the down-probability the UI claims to be a buy/sell signal is silently dropped — likely an intended bar/label was lost.
fix: Either remove probDown or surface it (e.g. show 'P(down) probDown%' next to the RF P(UP) stat).

title: Command-bar search can flash stale results after Enter navigates away
description: handleCmdInput debounces the /api/search fetch (searchTimer, 300ms). On Enter it hides the dropdown, clears the input and calls openResearch, but it does NOT clearTimeout(searchTimer). A search fetch already scheduled/in-flight from the keystrokes before Enter can resolve afterward and call el.classList.add('visible'), re-showing the results dropdown over the research view the user just opened.
fix: In the Enter branch (and Escape branch) call clearTimeout(searchTimer) before returning, and/or guard the async handler with a generation counter so a late response can't re-show the dropdown.

title: Options expiry <option> values injected unescaped (minor, low-trust source)
description: selectEl.innerHTML = dates.map(d => '<option value="' + d + '">' + d + '</option>') interpolates the raw date strings d into both the attribute and text without _esc. Dates come from the upstream options provider (yfinance) so the practical risk is low, but it's an inconsistency: every other API-text interpolation in this file routes through _esc, and a date string containing a quote/bracket would break the <select> markup.
fix: Escape: `'<option value="' + _esc(d) + '">' + _esc(d) + '</option>'`.

title: Dashboard 'Positions' and 'Win rate' KPIs stay '—' whenever the analytics fetch fails
description: The dashboard KPI tiles aj-kpi-positions and aj-kpi-winrate are only populated inside the analytics try-block (lines 4729-4730). If /api/aj/analytics throws (caught at 4759, which only writes 'Analytics unavailable.' into aj-analytics), these two header KPIs are left showing the placeholder '—' even though /api/aj/status already returned position/order data that could populate them. Mild but the dashboard looks broken when one sub-endpoint is down.
fix: Seed the KPIs from the already-fetched status payload (e.g. orders/positions counts from s) as a fallback, or set them to '—' explicitly only in the catch so a partial failure degrades gracefully.

title: Equity-chart empty-state overwrites the canvas's parent innerHTML, removing the canvas permanently for that render
description:
When eqRows.length < 2, the code does cc.parentNode.innerHTML = '
No equity history…
', which destroys the node. That's fine for the current render, but because loadTradingView re-runs analytics on every refresh without re-rendering the dashboard HTML in this branch path is only safe because the whole view is rebuilt each loadTradingView. If any future code re-invokes only the analytics block (e.g. a partial refresh), the canvas would already be gone and createEquityChart('aj-equity-chart',…) would silently no-op. Latent fragility.
fix: Replace only the canvas's own contents/visibility (e.g. hide the canvas and insert a sibling message) rather than blowing away parentNode.innerHTML, so the canvas element survives for subsequent renders.

title: Analytics profit_factor and Sharpe rendered as raw floats (can show long decimals or 'Infinity')
description: The analytics statline prints ${ts.profit_factor == null ? '—' : ts.profit_factor} and ${sh.sharpe == null ? '—' : sh.sharpe} directly, bypassing fmt.num. A profit_factor with no losing trades can be a very large number or Infinity (JSON null vs Infinity aside), and Sharpe can be a long float like 1.7320508…, producing ugly/overflowing values in the KPI strip.
fix: Format both through the numeric helper, e.g. fmt.num(ts.profit_factor) and fmt.num(sh.sharpe), guarding null first.

title: Contagion graph company name, sector and filing date rendered unescaped
description: mapContagion() escapes the per-row connection fields (ticker/name/relationship/context) but the KPI header cells inject data.company_name||data.company, data.sector and data.filing_date with no _esc, from /api/contagion.
fix: Escape these three: _esc(data.company_name||data.company||symbol), _esc(data.sector||'—'), _esc(data.filing_date||'—').

title: GEX gamma-wall type label rendered unescaped
description: analyzeGex() escapes nothing for w.type in the gamma walls table: '...' + (w.type || '—') + '...'. The strike/gex are numbers (safe via _alphaFmtNum) but w.type is a raw string from /api/gex/<symbol> placed inside a signal-badge span.
fix: Use _esc(w.type || '—') for the badge text.

title: Forecast horizon read as string; query default differs from select
description: analyzeForecast() does `var horizon = hsel ? hsel.value : 20;` — hsel.value is the string '20', and when the select is absent the fallback is the number 20. The value is only concatenated into the URL so it works, but if a caller passes sym programmatically before the view DOM exists, horizon becomes 20 (number) vs '20' (string) inconsistently. Minor, but the bigger issue is no validation that hsel.value is one of the allowed horizons.
fix: Normalize: var horizon = parseInt(hsel && hsel.value, 10) || 20; before building the URL.

title: Several alpha analyzers lack the results.isConnected post-fetch guard used by their siblings
description: analyzeGex/mapContagion/nowcastAltData correctly check `if (!results.isConnected) return;` after the await to avoid writing into a detached node when the user navigates away mid-fetch. But analyzeSyntheticInsider (8272), scanSyntheticInsiderPortfolio (8341), detectReflexivity (8405) and loadLiquidityData (8528) omit this guard. On slow responses they will overwrite results.innerHTML after the view changed, or write into a node that was replaced — at minimum wasted work, at worst stale content flashes in the wrong view.
fix: Add `if (!results.isConnected) return;` immediately after each `await API.get(...)` in those four functions, matching the guarded siblings.

title: Social Pulse Wikipedia stats call .toLocaleString on possibly-non-number values
description: renderSocialPulse() does ws.latest != null ? ws.latest.toLocaleString('en-US') : '—' and Math.round(ws.baseline_7d). If the API returns these as numeric strings (common with loosely-typed JSON pipelines) .toLocaleString still works but Math.round('123') coerces — however if latest is an object/array the call throws and the whole Social Pulse panel falls into the catch showing 'Social pulse unavailable'. The latest path has no Number() coercion unlike _fmtScanPrice elsewhere.
fix: Coerce defensively: Number(ws.latest).toLocaleString(...) guarded by Number.isFinite, e.g. Number.isFinite(+ws.latest) ? (+ws.latest).toLocaleString('en-US') : '—'.

title: Cache-busting version query strings are hand-maintained and drift between files
description: terminal.css?v=19, app.js?v=29, jarvis.js?v=22, charts.js?v=4 and the v=1 research/synth modules are versioned by hand. The research/synth modules are pinned at ?v=1 despite app.js being at v=29; any edit to those modules will be served stale from cache to returning users because the query string never changed. This is a real correctness/deploy hazard for a frequently-edited frontend.
fix: Drive the version suffix from app_version (already templated at line 345) or a build hash, e.g. src="/static/js/research_backtest.js?v={{ app_version }}", so every module busts cache together on release.

title: Alt-data beat probability mixes percent and fraction without normalization
description: nowcastAltData() treats beat_probability as a 0-100 number for the color thresholds (>=60 positive, >=40 amber) and renders _alphaFmtNum(beatProb,1)+'%'. If the backend ever returns a 0..1 fraction (as other endpoints in this file do, e.g. prob_up), every value < 1 would be classed col-negative and shown as e.g. '0.7%'. Worth confirming the contract; the percent-vs-fraction ambiguity is a known bug class here.
fix: Normalize once: if typeof beatProb==='number' && beatProb<=1, multiply by 100 before thresholding/formatting, or document/assert the 0-100 contract at the call site.
